accepted_edits.reason: the edit adds exactly the fence and fourth case the acted reasoning answer promised

findings.reason: as written the node's fix converts a stranded run into a possible two-worker run in one worktree, so the endpoint (free the hold without admitting a second launch) must gain a fence on the released holder or the plan ships a worse defect than the one it repairs.
findings.text: §28 frees a live holder's reservation at a bound of at least 15 minutes and asserts "a relaunch of the run is admitted", but nothing then stops the aged-out launch from continuing into its own spawn: `supervised_launch` reserves at dispatch_launch.py:3197 and only records a supervisor after `_start_supervisor` returns, so a holder that wakes after the release passes every guard (the spawn guard admits the attempt its own reservation covers) and two workers run in one worktree. `reservation_in_flight` states the invariant the plan overturns — "while it lives the launch is in flight, including a launch still waiting for a scheduler slot, so age is never a reason to free it" (dispatch_launch.py:2428-2430) — and the reservation's own introducing commit d36e465b39 records "it is never freed by age" because two doors preparing one attempt is the defect the reservation was built to stop, while §28's own evidence shows the holder sat in D state for 1 h 50 min. §25 handles the analogous window by reading the refusal record again after the spawn; §28 needs the equivalent for an aged-out reservation, or the bound must be justified against a holder that resumes

findings.reason: the diagnosis is a manifest obligation rather than a property of the code, and the two mechanisms are each independently measured by the three cases, so adding a check for it would not change what the plan delivers.
findings.text: §28's Deliverable requires the node to establish from the run directory and the station's stderr whether the launch raised, returned early or hung, and record it, but the three done-when cases address only the two repairs; a node could skip the diagnosis entirely and still pass the gate, even though which of the two fixes is needed depends on that answer

response_events.note: The age release is now paired with a fence: before _start_supervisor, a launch re-reads its reservation under the reservation lock and proceeds only while its attempt is still the newest; a launch whose hold was released and relaunched abandons, writes its exit receipt and spawns nothing. A fourth done-when case asserts that an aged-out launch woken after a relaunch starts no supervisor. reservation_in_flight's docstring is revised to state the new rule.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `held_launch_reservation` (dispatch_launch.py:2468), `_reserved_attempt_ended` (:2443), `reservation_in_flight` (:2423) and `STEP_WAIT_CEILING_SECONDS` (:4268) all resolve where §28 names them, and the cited run directory `r-20261112T131432188244-review-of-sweep-never-waits-on-a-promotion-5bc11377cbc0` holds exactly the records §28 describes (`attempt-1.reservation` naming pid 3815542 with `supervisor_pid` null at 13:23:10Z, `prompt.txt` and `harness/` at 13:24Z, no `stream.jsonl`, `stderr.log`, `worker.json` or `supervisor.json`).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §28's third case ("the same reservation within the bound, or one with a recorded live supervisor, is still held") is sound, but the deliverable's first clause, that the node establishes and records whether the launch raised, returned early or hung, is measured by no case.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the three cases run on a temporary crew home, each arm's log sits under the run directory and opens with its revision and literal command, and the fragment is a durable path under the plan's evidence directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §28 names no new symbol carrying a plan label or ticket number, and its prose states mechanisms rather than a changelog of the incident.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the age bound releases the hold while the reserving process may still be alive and later spawn, and §28 states no fence on that launch, so the node reintroduces the duplicate-worker race the reservation exists to prevent.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — both mechanisms serve one endpoint, a launch that never reached its worker stops holding its run, and each has its own case; the exit receipt covers a launch that ended and the bound covers one that hung, so one verdict closes both.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s28 declares no upstream and consumes nothing from an open section; its two mechanisms sit in `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py`, whose §27 change has landed at 64a1b15414 (verified with `git cat-file -t`).
